s.g: Suffix used to form verbs from nouns, and sometimes from adjectives.
perfect pitch (ability to identify a note by name on hearing it, or to re-create a specified note from memory, without the benefit of an externally provided reference pitch)
update (action of making something up to date)
Appalachians (a mountain range in eastern North America)
a genius (someone possessing extraordinary mental capacity)
one can, one may, one is allowed to
some (implies that one knows who or what, but is deliberately refraining from naming who or what)
blasphemy, sacrilege (desecration, profanation, misuse or violation of something sacred)
megatsunami (an extremely large tsunami-like wave caused by an avalanche or landslide displacing large amounts of water very quickly)
to be pictured, to appear (in one's imagination)
to show up (to appear suddenly or unexpectedly)
natively, naturally, as found in nature (about a chemical, protein, etc.)
natively (in a manner present from birth)
natively (in a manner designed for a particular platform)
perplexedly, in perplexity, with a puzzled look
Panama City (the capital city of the country of Panama)
to hem a quilted lining under (something)
to get intoxicated (with joy, success etc)
to spread, to run, to blur
to run to fat, to grow obese
contraction (a strong and often painful shortening of the uterine muscles prior to or during childbirth)
already; carries the sense of the perfect continuous tenses in English.
Used to emphasise an amount or quantity of something; now, already, as early as, as late as, as recently as

ulus, uls (various historical or modern Turkic or Mongolian regions)
